prior.text:
仅凭已有知识可以这样回答：

1. **工具定位**：CUDA 11 起官方调试工具是 `compute-sanitizer`，取代已废弃的 `cuda-memcheck`（后者在 CUDA 11.x 中被标记 deprecated，其后版本移除）。两者都包含 memcheck 子工具，专门检测 illegal memory access / 越界访问。
2. **基本用法**：`compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck ./myApp`（默认工具就是 memcheck，可直接 `compute-sanitizer ./myApp`）。旧写法：`cuda-memcheck --tool memcheck ./myApp`。
3. **定位到行的关键前提**：编译 kernel 时加源码行信息，即 nvcc 加 `-lineinfo`（轻量，不影响优化）或 `-G`（完整调试信息，会显著降低性能）。不加的话报告里只有 SASS 地址，没有 .cu 文件行号。
4. **报告内容**：memcheck 会打印错误类型（如 "Invalid __global__ read of size 4"）、出错的线程块/线程坐标、地址，以及（在有行信息时）kernel 名 + 源文件:行号，还有 host 侧调用栈（哪个 launch 触发）。
5. **常用参数**（不完全确定，需核实）：`--show-backtrace`、`--launch-timeout`、`--destroy-on-device-error`、`--save <file>` 保存输出；`--print-limit` 限制错误条数。
6. 可配合 `cuda-gdb` 进一步精确定位。

不确定处：
- 具体输出字段的官方措辞与新版格式（如 backtrace 的展示级别 user/demangled/raw）。
- `--save`、`--print-limit` 等旗标的准确拼写与默认值。
- compute-sanitizer 文档中关于 "Address ... is out of bounds" 上下文段落的准确描述。
- cuda-memcheck 被移除的确切 CUDA 版本。

**标题**: NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer | NVIDIA Developer

[](https://developer.nvidia.com/compute-sanitizer)

# NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer

## Compute Sanitizer Tools & API

**Compute Sanitizer** is a functional correctness checking suite. This suite contains multiple tools that can perform different type of checks. Tool features are described below.

The **Compute Sanitizer API** enables the creation of sanitizing and tracing tools that target CUDA applications. Examples of such tools are memory and race condition checkers. The Compute Sanitizer API is composed of three APIs: the callback API, the patching API and the memory API. It is delivered as a dynamic library on supported platforms.

### [Memcheck](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/sanitizer-docs/ComputeSanitizer/index.html#memcheck-tool)

The *memcheck* tool is a run time error detection tool for CUDA applications. The tool can precisely detect and report out of bounds and misaligned memory accesses to global, local and shared memory in CUDA applications. It can also detect and report hardware reported error information. In addition, the memcheck tool can detect and report memory leaks in the user application.

### [Racecheck](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/sanitizer-docs/ComputeSanitizer/index.html#racecheck-tool)

The *racecheck* tool is a run time shared memory data access hazard detector. The primary use of this tool is to help identify memory access race conditions in CUDA applications that use shared memory.

In CUDA applications, storage declared with the *__shared__* qualifier is placed on chip *shared memory*. All threads in a thread block can access this per block shared memory. Shared memory goes out of scope when the thread block completes execution. As shared memory is on chip, it is frequently used for inter-thread communication and as a temporary buffer to hold data being processed. As this data is being accessed by multiple threads in parallel, incorrect program assumptions may result in data races. Racecheck is a tool built to identify these hazards and help users write programs free of shared memory races.

Currently, this tool only supports detecting accesses to on-chip shared memory.

### [Initcheck](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/sanitizer-docs/ComputeSanitizer/index.html#initcheck-tool)

The *initcheck* tool is a run time uninitialized device global memory access detector. This tool can identify when device global memory is accessed without it being initialized via device side writes, or via CUDA memcpy and memset API calls.

Currently, this tool only supports detecting accesses to device global memory.

### [Synccheck](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/sanitizer-docs/ComputeSanitizer/index.html#synccheck-tool)

The *synccheck* tool is a runtime tool that can identify whether a CUDA application is correctly using synchronization primitives, specifically __syncthreads() and *__syncwarp()* intrinsics and their Cooperative Groups API counterparts.

### Developer Benefits

**Compute Sanitizer**: Provides the ability to ensure the code correctness of your GPU accelerated kernels  
**Compute Sanitizer API**: Provides the ability to incorporate GPU code correctness into your own tools

**Both the Compute Sanitizer suite and API are available in the CUDA Toolkit. You may obtain the latest version of Compute Sanitizer by downloading the CUDA Toolkit**

  [Download the CUDA Toolkit Now](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads) 

##### [Sanitizer Tools documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/sanitizer-docs/ComputeSanitizer/index.html)  |   [Sanitizer API documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/sanitizer-docs/SanitizerApiGuide/index.html)  |   [Revision History](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/sanitizer-docs/ReleaseNotes/index.html)

**NVIDIA® Compute Sanitizer** is freely offered through the [NVIDIA Registered Developer Program](https://developer.nvidia.com/sign-up-gameworks-registered-developer-program) and as part of the [CUDA Toolkit](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-toolkit)

# Extracted from Compute Sanitizer Documentation

Below are verbatim extracts organized by your five requests, with the original section titles noted. **Note on item (5):** the provided documentation contains **no statement** about cuda-memcheck being deprecated/replaced — see the final section for details.

---

## 1. Invoking compute-sanitizer and the memcheck tool

### Section: "## Compute Sanitizer"

> Compute Sanitizer tools can be invoked by running the `compute-sanitizer` executable as follows:

```
compute-sanitizer [options] app_name [app_options]
```

> For a full list of options that can be specified to compute-sanitizer and their default values, see Command Line Options

### Section: "## Memcheck Tool" → "### Using Memcheck"

> The memcheck tool is enabled by default when running the Compute Sanitizer application. It can also be explicitly enabled by using the `--tool memcheck` option.

```
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck [sanitizer_options] app_name [app_options]
```

> When run in this way, the memcheck tool will look for precise, imprecise, malloc/free and CUDA API errors. The reporting of device leaks must be explicitly enabled. Errors identified by the memcheck tool are displayed on the screen after the application has completed execution.

### Section: "### How to Get Compute Sanitizer"

> Compute Sanitizer is installed as part of the CUDA toolkit.

---

## 2. Getting source line information for errors

### Section: "### Compilation Options"

> The Compute Sanitizer tools do not need any special compilation flags to function.
>
> The output displayed by the Compute Sanitizer tools is more useful with some extra compiler flags. The `-G` option to nvcc forces the compiler to generate debug information for the CUDA application. To generate line number information for applications without affecting the optimization level of the output, the `-lineinfo` nvcc option can be used. The Compute Sanitizer tools fully support both of these options and can display source attribution of errors for applications compiled with line information.
>
> For memcheck specifically, the `-fdevice-sanitize=memcheck` option enables compile-time instrumentation, which provides significant performance improvements and enhanced error detection through base-and-bounds analysis. This flag instruments the code at compile time rather than at runtime.

> **Note**
>
> Option `-fdevice-sanitize=memcheck` does not imply the generation of debug information. To get source attribution of errors, the application must also be compiled with `-lineinfo` or `-G`.

> Sample command line to build with function symbols and device-side line information on Linux:

```
nvcc -Xcompiler -rdynamic -lineinfo  -o out in.cu
```

> Sample command line to build with compile-time memcheck instrumentation and device-side line information:

```
nvcc -fdevice-sanitize=memcheck -lineinfo -o out in.cu
```

### Related statement from "### Supported Error Detection"

> Precise errors in memcheck are those that the tool can uniquely identify and gather all information for. For these errors, memcheck can report the block and thread coordinates of the thread causing the failure, the program counter (PC) of the instruction performing the access, as well as the address being accessed and its size and type. If the CUDA application contains line number information (by either being compiled with device side debugging information, or with line information), then the tool will also print the source file and line number of the erroneous access.

---

## 3. Memcheck error report format (file/line attribution)

### Section: "### Understanding Memcheck Errors" — "1. Memory access error"

> Memory access errors are generated for errors that the memcheck tool can correctly attribute and identify the erroneous instruction. Below is an example of a precise memory access error.

```
========= Invalid __global__ write of size 4 bytes
=========     at unaligned_kernel():0x160 in memcheck_demo.cu:6
=========     by thread (0,0,0) in block (0,0,0)
=========     Address 0x7f6510c00001 is misaligned
```

**Line-by-line explanation (verbatim excerpts):**

> **The first line** shows the memory segment, type and size being accessed. The memory segment is one of:
> - `__global__` : for device global memory
> - `__shared__` : for per block shared memory
> - `__local__` : for per thread local memory

> **The second line** contains the CUDA kernel name, offset of the instruction, **the source file and line number (if available)**. In this example, the instruction causing the access was at offset 0x160 inside the `unaligned_kernel` CUDA kernel. Additionally, since the application was compiled with line number information, this instruction corresponds to line 6 in the memcheck_demo.cu source file.

> **The third line** contains the thread indices and block indices of the thread on which the error was hit.

> **The fourth line** contains the memory address being accessed and the type of access error. The type of access error can either be out of bounds access or misaligned access.

**Malloc/free error example (same section):**

```
========= Malloc/Free error encountered : Double free
=========     at 0x79d8
=========     by thread (0,0,0) in block (0,0,0)
=========     Address 0x400aff920
```

### Section: "#### `memcheck_demo` Output with Memcheck (Release Build)" (Compute Sanitizer Tool Examples)

> In this case, since the application is built in release mode, the Compute Sanitizer output contains only the kernel names from the application causing the access violation. Though the kernel name and error type are detected, **there is no line number information on the failing kernel**. Also included in the output are the host and device backtraces for the call sites where the functions were launched

---

## 4. Command line options relevant to locating errors

### Table 2. Backtrace options

| Option | Values | Default | Description (verbatim) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `show-backtrace` | yes, host, device, no | yes | "Displays a backtrace for most types of errors. 'no' disables all backtraces, 'yes' enables all backtraces. 'host' enables only host side backtraces. 'device' enables only device side backtraces." |
| `backtrace-short` | yes, no | yes | "Short version of backtrace is used. CUDART frames and frames below main() are not printed." |

### Table 1. Compute Sanitizer command line options (error-location-relevant selections)

| Option | Values | Default | Description (verbatim) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `save` | {filename} | N/A | "Filename where Compute Sanitizer will save the output from the current run." |
| `log-file` | {filename} | N/A | "This is the file Compute Sanitizer will write all of its text output to. By default, Compute Sanitizer will print all output to stdout." |
| `print-limit` | {number} | 100 | "When this option is set, Compute Sanitizer will stop printing errors after reaching the given number of errors. Use 0 for unlimited printing." |
| `print-level` | info, auto, warn, error, fatal | auto | "Set the minimum level of errors to print. 'auto' defaults to 'warn', but changes to 'info' when –dump-kernel-launches is enabled." |
| `num-callers-device` | {number} | 0 | "Set the number of callers to print in device stack traces. Use 0 for unlimited." |
| `num-callers-host` | {number} | 0 | "Set the number of callers to print in host stack traces. Use 0 for unlimited." |
| `dump-kernel-launches` | N/A | disabled | "Dumps information for all kernel launches including name, launch number, dimensions, stream, and host backtrace. Both filtered and unfiltered launches are reported with indication of filter status." |
| `demangle` | full, simple, no | full | "Enables the demangling of device function names." |
| `strip-paths` | yes, no | yes | "Print only filenames instead of full paths." |
| `prefix` | {string} | `========` | "The string prepended to Compute Sanitizer output lines." |
| `generate-coredump` | N/A | disabled | "When this is set, a coredump will be generated for the first error encountered and program execution will be stopped." |
| `coredump-name` | {filename} | N/A | "Name to use for the generated coredump file." |
| `error-exitcode` | {number} | 0 | "The exit code Compute Sanitizer will return if the original application succeeded but the tool detected that errors were present. This is meant to allow Compute Sanitizer to be integrated into automated test suites." |
| `launch-count (c)` | {number} | 0 | "Limit the number of kernel launches to check. The count is only incremented for launches that match the kernel filters. Use 0 for unlimited." |
| `launch-skip (s)` | {number} | 0 | "Set the number of kernel launches to skip before starting to check." |
| `kernel-name` / `kernel-name-exclude` | {key1=val1}[{,key2=val2}] | N/A | "Controls which application kernels will be checked by the running the Compute Sanitizer tool." |

### Section: "### Stack Backtraces"

> Compute Sanitizer can generate backtraces when given `--show-backtrace` option. Backtraces usually consist of two sections – a saved host backtrace that leads up to the CUDA driver call site, and a device backtrace at the time of the error. Each backtrace contains a list of frames showing the state of the stack at the time the backtrace was created.
>
> To get function names in the host backtraces, the user application must be built with support for symbol information in the host application.

Per **Table 8**, a "Memory access error" yields a "Kernel launch on host" host backtrace and a "Precise backtrace on device"; a "cudaMalloc allocation leak" yields the "Callsite of cudaMalloc."

### Section: "### Escape Sequences" (for `--save` and `--log-file` filenames)

> - `%%` : Replaced with a literal %.
> - `%p` : Replaced with the PID of the Compute Sanitizer frontend application.
> - `%q{ENVVAR}` : Replaced with the contents of the environment variable `ENVVAR`. If the variable does not exist, this is replaced with an empty string.
> - Any other character following the % causes an error.

---

## 5. Statement about cuda-memcheck being deprecated/replaced

**No such statement exists in the provided documentation.** The text does not mention `cuda-memcheck` (the legacy standalone tool) at all, nor does it contain any deprecation or replacement notice. The only related availability statement is from "### How to Get Compute Sanitizer":

> Compute Sanitizer is installed as part of the CUDA toolkit.

---

## Key Takeaways

- **Basic usage:** `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck [sanitizer_options] app_name [app_options]` (memcheck is the default tool).
- **For file/line attribution:** compile with `-lineinfo` (no optimization impact) or `-G` (full debug info); e.g., `nvcc -Xcompiler -rdynamic -lineinfo -o out in.cu`. Without these, reports show only kernel names/offsets.
- **Error reports** attribute errors as `at <kernel_name>():<offset> in <file.cu>:<line>`.
- **Locating errors further:** use `--show-backtrace`, `--num-callers-host/device`, `--save`/`--log-file`, `--print-limit 0` for unlimited error output, and `--generate-coredump` for post-mortem debugging.
- **cuda-memcheck deprecation is not addressed** in this document.

**No statement about cuda-memcheck/CUDA-MEMCHECK being deprecated exists in this document, and no statement about compute-sanitizer exists beyond a version listing.** I searched the entire CUDA 11.6 Release Notes content, including the "Deprecated Features" section (Section 1.6), and found no such statement.

## What the Deprecated Features Section Actually Contains (Section 1.6)

The only items listed under "Deprecated Features" → "General CUDA" are:

1. **`cudaDeviceSynchronize()` deprecation** — related to on-device fork/join parallelism:
   > "The `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` function used for on-device fork/join parallelism is deprecated in preparation for a replacement programming model with higher performance."

2. **CentOS Linux 8 support deprecation**:
   > "CentOS Linux 8 has reached End-of-Life on Dec 31, 2021 and support for this OS is now deprecated in the CUDA Toolkit. CentOS Linux 8 support will be completely removed in a future release."

Other deprecated features in the document relate to cuBLAS, cuFFT, cuSOLVER, cuSPARSE, CUDA Math APIs, and nvJPEG — **none mention cuda-memcheck or compute-sanitizer**.

## The Only Mentions Found (Neither Is a Deprecation Statement)

Both tools appear **only** in Table 1 ("CUDA 11.6 Component Versions"), as simple version listings:

| Component Name | Version | Supported Architectures |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA Memcheck | 11.6.55 | x86_64, POWER |
| CUDA Compute Sanitizer API | 11.6.55 | x86_64, POWER, Arm64 |

These entries simply indicate that both CUDA Memcheck and the Compute Sanitizer API are shipped as toolkit components at version 11.6.55 in this release — they carry no deprecation notice, replacement recommendation, or commentary of any kind.

## Conclusion

To be explicit: **the CUDA 11.6 Release Notes contain no verbatim statement about cuda-memcheck/CUDA-MEMCHECK being deprecated, nor any statement (beyond the version table entry) about compute-sanitizer.** If you're looking for the cuda-memcheck deprecation announcement (which NVIDIA made in favor of compute-sanitizer), it does not appear in this particular release notes document and would need to be located elsewhere (e.g., the CUDA Toolkit Installation Guide or the compute-sanitizer documentation).

# 用 compute-sanitizer 定位 CUDA kernel 越界访问的行号

## 1. 工具与版本关系

- `cuda-memcheck` 已从 CUDA 12.0 移除，官方替代品是 **Compute Sanitizer**。官方原文（CUDA 12.0 Release Notes, Deprecated Features）：

> "CUDA-MEMCHECK is removed from CUDA 12.0, and has been replaced with Compute Sanitizer."

- Compute Sanitizer 随 CUDA Toolkit 一起安装（"Compute Sanitizer is installed as part of the CUDA toolkit."）。CUDA 11.x 时代两者并存（11.6 组件表同时列出 CUDA Memcheck 11.6.55 与 Compute Sanitizer）；12.0+ 只能用 `compute-sanitizer`。

## 2. 关键前提：编译时加行号信息（不加就看不到 .cu 行号）

工具本身不需要特殊编译旗标就能运行，但要定位到**源码行**，必须加 `-lineinfo`（不影响优化，推荐）或 `-G`（完整调试信息，性能开销大）：

```bash
nvcc -Xcompiler -rdynamic -lineinfo -o out in.cu
```

- `-lineinfo`：生成行号信息，不改变优化级别
- `-G`：生成完整设备调试信息（设备 backtrace 可显示完整帧）
- `-Xcompiler -rdynamic`：保留 host 函数符号，使 host backtrace 显示函数名（Linux；Windows 用 `/Zi`）

官方原文：**"The Compute Sanitizer tools fully support both of these options and can display source attribution of errors for applications compiled with line information."** 以及："If the CUDA application contains line number information … then the tool will also print the source file and line number of the erroneous access."

## 3. 运行

```bash
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck ./out
# memcheck 是默认工具，可简写为：
compute-sanitizer ./out
```

旧版（CUDA < 12.0）等价写法：`cuda-memcheck --tool memcheck ./out`

## 4. 读报告：行号在哪里

官方示例输出（越界/未对齐访问）：

```
========= Invalid __global__ write of size 4 bytes
=========     at unaligned_kernel():0x160 in memcheck_demo.cu:6
=========     by thread (0,0,0) in block (0,0,0)
=========     Address 0x7f6510c00001 is misaligned
```

- 第 1 行：访问的内存段（`__global__` / `__shared__` / `__local__`）、读/写、字节数
- 第 2 行：**kernel 名 + 指令偏移 + 源文件:行号（`memcheck_demo.cu:6` 即越界语句所在行）**——前提是编译加了 `-lineinfo`/`-G`；release 不加行信息时这里只有 kernel 名和偏移，没有行号
- 第 3 行：出错线程坐标 (x,y,z) 与 block 坐标
- 第 4 行：被访问的地址及错误类型（out of bounds / misaligned）

报告还会附 host backtrace（指向触发该 kernel launch 的调用点）和 device backtrace，可以直接看到是源码哪个文件哪一行发起的 launch。

## 5. 常用辅助参数（官方 Command Line Options 表）

| 参数 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `--show-backtrace yes\|host\|device\|no` | yes | 显示/关闭回溯 |
| `--save <file>` / `--log-file <file>` | stdout | 保存输出到文件 |
| `--print-limit <n>` | 100 | 最多打印 n 条错误（0 = 不限）|
| `--num-callers-host/device <n>` | 0（不限）| 回溯打印的帧数 |
| `--kernel-name <...>` | — | 只检查匹配的 kernel（避免无关 kernel 刷屏）|
| `--launch-skip <s>` / `--launch-count <c>` | 0 | 跳过/限定检查的 launch 数 |
| `--generate-coredump` | off | 首个错误处生成 CUDA coredump 并停止（CUDA ≥ 11.6），可用 cuda-gdb 事后分析 |
| `--error-exitcode <n>` | 0 | 便于集成进自动化测试 |

## 6. 进阶（较新 CUDA）：编译期插桩，更快更准

```bash
nvcc -fdevice-sanitize=memcheck -lineinfo -o out in.cu
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck ./out
```

官方说明：`-fdevice-sanitize=memcheck` 提供显著性能提升和基于 base-and-bounds 的增强检测；注意它**不隐含生成调试信息**，要行号定位仍必须同时加 `-lineinfo` 或 `-G`。编译期 patching 要求 PTX 编译器与 compute-sanitizer 来自**同一 CUDA toolkit 版本**。直接用 ptxas 时等价旗标为 `-sanitize=memcheck`。

## 排查流程小结

1. `nvcc -Xcompiler -rdynamic -lineinfo -o app app.cu`（需要完整调试用 `-G`）
2. `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck ./app`
3. 看输出第 2 行 `at kernel():offset in file.cu:LINE` → 即越界语句
4. 用第 3 行线程/block 坐标推出出错的索引计算（如 `tid >= N` 未防护）
5. 报告太长时加 `--print-limit 0 --save out.log`、`--kernel-name` 过滤；难复现的挂 `--generate-coredump`

## 来源

- Compute Sanitizer 官方文档（CUDA 文档集）：https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/sanitizer-docs/ComputeSanitizer/index.html
- Compute Sanitizer 官方文档（新版路径）：https://docs.nvidia.com/compute-sanitizer/ComputeSanitizer/index.html
- NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer 产品页：https://developer.nvidia.com/compute-sanitizer
- CUDA 12.0 Release Notes（cuda-memcheck 移除声明）：https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.0.0/cuda-toolkit-release-notes/index.html
- CUDA 11.6 Release Notes（确认该版本两者并存、无弃用声明）：https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/11.6.0/cuda-toolkit-release-notes/index.html

## 无法核实处

- "cuda-memcheck 在 CUDA 11.6 被标记 deprecated" 的说法仅见于第三方（CSDN），本轮未在官方 11.6 Release Notes 中找到该声明；官方确证的只有"12.0 移除、由 Compute Sanitizer 取代"。
- compute-sanitizer 首次随哪个 CUDA 版本引入，本轮未取得官方原文。
- 第二个官方文档页返回末尾标注 `[content truncated]`，截断部分内容（可能含示例/版本信息）未取得。
- 以上命令均未实际运行（仅内容核查，非复现验证）。
</answer>
